raw_case_text:
A 76-year-old woman with stable RA developed malaise and a high-grade fever (>39.0 C) 5 days after receiving a second dose of BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine. Ten days after vaccination, she developed a persistent cough and dyspnea. Seventeen days after vaccination, she was admitted to another hospital because of persistent fever. Blood tests showed a white blood cell (WBC) count of 4990/muL and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels of 477 U/L and 6.4 mg/dL, respectively. Although the antigen test for SARS, serum B-D glucan, and blood culture was negative, tests for Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, and sputum culture were not examined. Chest computed tomography (CT) showed infiltration and ground glass opacites (GGOs) in all lung fields (Figure 1(a)). The patient was provisionally diagnosed with interstitial lung disease (ILD) and was transferred to our hospital 21 days after vaccination.
Prior to the onset of her symptoms, the patient's RA had been stable on methotrexate treatment (12 mg/week), which she had taken for 15 years.
On admission, her body temperature, blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, and SpO2 were 36.5 C, 110/60 mmHg, 65 beats/min, 18 breaths/min, and 98% (in room air), respectively. Her arthritis was stable and showed no changes of note since a previous check-up one month earlier. The results of blood tests were as follows: WBC, 5420/muL; red blood cells (RBC), 377 x 104/muL; hemoglobin (Hb), 11.2 g/dL; hematocrit, 35.5%; platelets, 40.4 x 104/muL; CRP 1.47 mg/dL; LDH, 311 U/L; Krebs von den Lungen-6 (KL-6), 452.4 U/mL; and surfactant protein D (SP-D), 226 ng/mL. Her rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and antinuclear antibody were negative.
Tests for Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, and tuberculosis (T-Spot), and antigen tests for Cryptococcus, Candida, Aspergillus, cytomegalovirus antigen, and SARS-CoV-2 antigen were negative. Serum beta-D glucan, blood culture, and polymerase chain reaction testing of respiratory samples for Pneumocystis jirovecii DNA were also negative. Chest CT showed a significant improvement compared to the chest CT performed 4 days earlier (Figure 1(b)). The patient was treated conservatively and did not receive antibiotics or immunosuppressive drugs during hospitalization. Her cough, dyspnea, and fever resolved spontaneously, and she was discharged from hospital after 7 days. Her final diagnosis was transient pneumonitis induced by a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. At the 3-month follow-up, she had not experienced a relapse of pneumonitis and her blood test results had improved: CRP, 0.06 mg/dL (from 1.47 mg/dL); LDH, 189 U/L (from 311 U/L); KL-6, 165.1 U/mL (from 452.4 U/mL); and SP-D, 102 ng/mL (from 226 ng/mL).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 76-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis stable on long-term methotrexate developed malaise and high fever (>39.0 °C) 5 days after her second BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, followed at day 10 by persistent cough and dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Maintained in stable remission on weekly methotrexate (12 mg/week) for 15 years for rheumatoid arthritis, the patient developed malaise and high-grade fever (>39.0 °C) 5 days after receiving her second dose of the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, followed 10 days post-vaccination by persistent cough and shortness of breath. She was hospitalized at an outside facility 17 days post-vaccination with diffuse ground-glass opacities on chest CT and transferred to our hospital at day 21.
subjective.past_medical_history: Rheumatoid arthritis stable for 15 years on methotrexate (12 mg/week); received second dose of BNT162b2 COVID-19 mRNA vaccine 21 days prior to transfer.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for post-vaccination malaise, high fever (>39.0 °C), cough, and dyspnea (all spontaneously improving by day 21 transfer); stable baseline joint status.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs on transfer (day 21 post-vaccination): Body temperature 36.5 °C, blood pressure 110/60 mmHg, pulse 65 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and room-air SpO2 98%; stable arthritis without synovitis flare.
objective.routine_investigations: Day 17 outside hospital labs: WBC 4,990/μL, LDH 477 U/L, CRP 6.4 mg/dL, negative SARS-CoV-2 antigen, and negative blood cultures. Day 21 transfer labs: WBC 5,420/μL, RBC 377 x 10^4/μL, hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, hematocrit 35.5%, platelets 40.4 x 10^4/μL, CRP 1.47 mg/dL (normalizing to 0.06 mg/dL at 3 months), LDH 311 U/L (189 U/L at 3 months), KL-6 452.4 U/mL (165.1 U/mL at 3 months), and surfactant protein D (SP-D) 226 ng/mL (102 ng/mL at 3 months); RF, anti-CCP, and ANA negative. Comprehensive microbiological screening: Negative Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, T-SPOT.TB, Cryptococcus, Candida, Aspergillus, CMV antigenemia, SARS-CoV-2 antigen, and blood cultures.
objective.advanced_workup: Fungal biomarker and Pneumocystis molecular testing: Negative serum beta-D-glucan (at both day 17 and day 21) and negative respiratory specimen Pneumocystis jirovecii DNA PCR. Serial chest CT scans: Day 17 chest CT demonstrated diffuse infiltrations and ground-glass opacities (GGOs) across all lung fields, which showed spontaneous marked regression on repeat chest CT 4 days later (day 21).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Self-limiting BNT162b2 COVID-19 mRNA vaccine-induced acute interstitial pneumonitis in a rheumatoid arthritis patient on long-term methotrexate, confirmed by temporal onset after the second vaccine dose, negative infectious workup (including negative Pneumocystis jirovecii PCR and serial beta-D-glucan assays), and spontaneous clinical, biomarker (CRP, LDH, KL-6, SP-D), and radiographic resolution without corticosteroid or antibiotic intervention. Plan and clinical course: Managed conservatively with close inpatient observation without antibiotics or corticosteroids; her fever, cough, and dyspnea resolved completely, she was discharged on hospital day 7, and she remained relapse-free with normalized KL-6 (165.1 U/mL) and SP-D (102 ng/mL) at 3-month follow-up.
